extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners (third-party submitters)
extracted.subtask_short: ex parte reexamination & prior art citation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, and processing prior-art citations, Section 301 written statements, and ex parte reexamination requests under U.S. law and USPTO rules. Covers content, form, timing, submission methods, processing, certificates, and procedural handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may cite prior art or written statements (35 U.S.C. 301)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person at any time may cite to the Office prior art consisting of patents or printed publications or statements of the patent owner filed in a proceeding before a Federal court or the Office in which the patent owner took a position on the scope of any claim of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “Any person” includes individuals, corporate or governmental entities, patentees, licensees, reexamination requesters, real parties in interest, persons without a real interest, and persons acting for real parties in interest. Examiners must not, on their own initiative, create and place submissions in patent files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirement: explanation of pertinence and manner of applying (35 U.S.C. 301 / 37 CFR 1.501)
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission must include an explanation in writing of the pertinence and manner of applying any cited prior art or written statement to at least one claim of the patent for the submission to be entered into the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanation must, for at least one claim, set forth how each cited item shows or teaches at least one claim limitation. Submissions by patent owners may also explain how claims differ from the cited art or statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 301 written statements identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission of a patent-owner written statement must identify: (i) the forum and proceeding in which the patent owner filed each statement; (ii) the specific papers and portions that contain the statement; and (iii) how each statement is one in which the patent owner took a position on the scope of any claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification can be aided by citing specific documents and page citations. Provide status of the proceeding and its relationship to the patent to assist the Office in readily identifying the statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/limitation of permissible submission content
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions under 37 CFR 1.501 are limited to patents, printed publications, patent owner written claim scope statements, accompanying information, and an explanation of pertinency and manner of applying them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must not include issues not directed to patents/printed publications/written claim scope statements — e.g., allegations under 35 U.S.C. 112, public use, conduct of the patent owner, or argument about prosecution history or references previously treated in prosecution/reexamination. If submission contains unauthorized content it should not be entered (return, discard, or close).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and translations to be submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of all cited prior-art patents or printed publications and any necessary English translations should be included so that the value of the citations can be readily determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of section 301 written statements and accompanying information must be submitted (redacted if subject to a protective order) to allow easy inspection and Office determination of claim meaning in subsequent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits, declarations, and evidentiary attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations or other written evidence relating to the submitted documents may accompany the 1.501 submission to explain contents or pertinent dates in more detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include commercial-success affidavits, declarations clarifying dates, or evidence addressing enablement/teaching of the cited art. Such evidence must still be directed to patents/printed publications/written statements and their pertinency.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fee required for 37 CFR 1.501 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission under 37 CFR 1.501 does not require payment of a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite no fee, submission must meet content and proof-of-service/formality requirements to be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof/certificate of service requirement for non-owner submissions (37 CFR 1.501(e), 1.248(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission by a person other than the patent owner must include certification that a copy of the submission was served in its entirety upon the patent owner at the correspondence address as provided in 37 CFR 1.33(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include proper proof of service will result in the submission not being entered into the patent file. Confidential submitters still must include proof of service; proof requirements are detailed in 37 CFR 1.248(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and anonymous submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon written request the identity of the person citing prior art or written statements may be excluded from the patent file and kept confidential; alternatively, submissions may be filed anonymously by omitting identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reexamination requesters, certification requirements and practitioner certifications interact with estoppel rules; real parties in interest may remain anonymous by using a registered practitioner who certifies compliance. Anonymous submitters should not identify themselves anywhere in their papers and must include proof of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing submissions under 35 U.S.C. 301
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may be filed 'at any time' defined as any time during the period of enforceability of a patent (generally patent term plus six years under 35 U.S.C. 286).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If litigation is instituted within the statute of limitations, submissions may be filed after expiration as long as the patent remains enforceable against someone. Submissions filed after an order to reexamine are stored until conclusion unless they meet specified exceptions (see handling rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry timing when a reexamination is pending (37 CFR 1.502 and 1.902)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations submitted after the date of an order to reexamine by persons other than the patent owner (or certain requesters) will have entry into the patent file delayed until the reexamination proceeding has been concluded by issuance of a reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.502 (ex parte) and 1.902 (inter partes) control processing. Some categories (patent owner, requester who submitted required fee and documents, certain replies, or enterable inter partes submissions) are exceptions and may be entered during reexamination. Submissions stored are not considered by the examiner during the reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of submission and electronic filing constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1.501 submission may be submitted via mail, hand-delivery, or via the USPTO patent electronic filing system if properly filed as a prior art submission and not as a follow-on paper. Design and plant patents cannot use USPTO e-filing for 1.501 submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions via the electronic system are reviewed for compliance prior to entry; misuse (e.g., entering as follow-on or by someone other than patent owner’s representative) may violate the electronic filing agreement and risk account revocation. Submissions forwarded to the Technology Center for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing responsibility and forwarding to Technology Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions received will be forwarded to the Technology Center that currently examines the technology where the patent is classified. The Technology Center must promptly determine whether the submission meets statutory and regulatory requirements and enter it into the patent file at the appropriate time if proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff review for compliance prior to entry; proper submissions filed after order for reexamination will be stored until conclusion, and patent owner and third-party submitter (if known) should be notified that the submission is stored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for ex parte reexamination requests (35 U.S.C. 302 and 37 CFR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for ex parte reexamination must meet formal requirements set by statute and regulation (content of request, fee, certification, representative information, showing of a substantial new question of patentability, copies of prior art, certificate of service, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter enumerates required sections for ex parte requests: persons who may file, representative of requester, content of request, fee, showing of substantial new question of patentability, statement applying prior art to claims, copies of prior art, certificate of service, amendments included by patent owner, address, withdrawal, correspondence, timeliness, and initial processing. Each of those items must be included and comply with the detailed rules (see the specific MPEP sections referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing a Substantial New Question of Patentability (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reexamination request must present a substantial new question of patentability as the basis for ordering ex parte reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requester must explain how the cited prior art raises a SNQ as to at least one claim; the request should set forth comparisons and reasoning (e.g., how references read on claim limitations or render them obvious). Specific criteria and examples are provided in the chapter (see MPEP § 2242 and related subsections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement Applying Prior Art in the Request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request should include a statement applying the cited prior art to the patent claims (showing how each reference pertains to claim limitations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear mappings of reference disclosures to claim limitations, including citations to figures/columns/lines where limitations are shown, and explain combinations relied on for obviousness arguments where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Service for reexamination requests and submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for reexamination and third-party submissions must include a certificate of service showing that a copy was served upon the patent owner at the correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate must comply with 37 CFR 1.248(b). Lack of proper proof of service can prevent entry or processing; confidential submitters must still demonstrate service or meet the exception rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments by the patent owner during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to claims or specification in the reexamination proceeding must be presented treating the changes made by any prior reexamination certificate as part of the original patent; italicized text in a certificate is considered originally present and bracketed text as not present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that re-add text already italicized in a certificate or otherwise improperly present certificate text as a new change are informal and noncompliant with 37 CFR 1.530; the examiner should notify the patent owner of the defect using Form PTOL-475 or PTO-2311 and set a time period to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination Certificate content and format (35 U.S.C. 307 / MPEP guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination certificate will identify the patent claims confirmed as patentable, canceled, disclaimed, and those not examined; new claims are printed completely in italics and amended claims printed with italics and bracketing indicating amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate title will indicate the type (e.g., 'Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate' and may state 'Ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257'). Certificates use kind-code suffixes (B/C plus an ordinal) to show sequence of reexamination certificates and include bibliographic data, representative claim, and notice that a list of cited prior art will be available via the USPTO electronic filing system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening rights resulting from reexamination (35 U.S.C. 307(b) / §252 analogy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amended or new claim determined to be patentable and incorporated into a patent following reexamination will have the same intervening-rights effect as specified in 35 U.S.C. 252 for reissued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons who made, purchased, used, or imported items or who made substantial preparation for an invention prior to issuance of the reexamination certificate may have intervening rights; see cited case law and statutory provisions for scope and application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways in which an ex parte reexamination proceeding may be concluded
rubrics_metrics.description: An ex parte reexamination may be concluded by (A) denial/vacation/termination without issuance of a certificate; (B) issuance of a reexamination certificate under 37 CFR 1.570(b); (C) conclusion by merger with a reissue proceeding where reissue patent serves as certificate; or (D) conclusion by merger with an inter partes reexamination and issuance of a single merged certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each conclusion path has specified processing steps (e.g., status codes, partial refunds under 37 CFR 1.26(c) where applicable, forwarding to CRU, printing/annotating PDP screens, scanning into IFW, and review by SPRS or QAS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination of a reexamination: basis for decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A later reexamination request filed on a patent for which a reexamination certificate has already issued (‘reexamination of a reexamination’) must be considered based on the patent claims as modified by the previously issued reexamination certificate, not based on the original claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When received, CRU support staff will print the issued reexamination certificate and make it of record as a preliminary amendment. The examiner must ensure certificate changes are properly entered so the reexamination is conducted on the accurate specification and claims; checklists (Form PTO-1516, PTO-1517) and supervisory review are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required forms and checklists for ex parte reexamination processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific USPTO forms must be used in ex parte reexamination actions (e.g., PTOL-471D/G for order/denial, PTOL-466 Office Action, PTOL-467 Advisory Action, PTOL-476 Reasons for Patentability/Confirmation, PTOL-465 transmittal, PTOL-474 interview summary, PTOL-1516 examiner checklist, PTOL-1517 reexamination clerk checklist, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the listed forms is mandatory for corresponding processing steps; a Request for Ex Parte Reexamination Transmittal Form (PTO/SB/57) is available but not mandatory. Checklists must be completed and reviewed by CRU SPRS or TC QAS and paralegal to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on examiner-initiated placement of submissions in patent file
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examiners should not, at their own initiative, create a submission under 35 U.S.C. 301 and place it in a patent file or forward it for placement in the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are delegated responsibility to make patentability decisions. Any activity by examiners that appears to indicate claims are not patentable outside the cases pending before them is inappropriate.
